overview.intro:
Chapter 35 covers protein and starch-based industrial and food ingredients: casein, caseinates and milk protein concentrate (3501), egg albumin and whey protein isolates (3502), gelatin and animal glues (3503), peptones and other proteins such as collagen and pea protein (3504), dextrins and modified starches (3505), prepared glues and adhesives (3506) and enzymes (3507). The U.S. imported **$3.95B** of them in 2025; enzymes were the largest product ($960M), led by Denmark.

Base rates are low — **8 of the 33 lines are Free**, most others are 2–6% or a few cents per kilogram — so the **extra duties decide the cost**. No Chapter 35 line is on the exemption lists of the 2026 Section 301 tariffs: EU goods pay 10% in total, Japan and South Korea 12.5% in total, New Zealand, Australia and most other suppliers +10% or +12.5%, Brazil +37.5%, and China +20% or +37.5%. Canadian casein, whey protein, gelatin, protein isolates and modified starches pay a **50% Section 338 duty even when they qualify for USMCA**. Pea protein from China and hard gelatin capsules from four countries also carry antidumping and countervailing duties, which are not in the tariff calculator.

workedExamples.title: 20 t of whey protein isolate from New Zealand
workedExamples.body: Whey protein concentrates of more than 80% whey protein (dry basis) are **Free** under the general rate, but New Zealand is one of the 60 economies in the 2026 Section 301 action, so the shipment pays **+12.5%** (9903.05.57). On a $300,000 entry that is **$37,500**. No Chapter 35 line is on the note 52(b) exemption list, and the United States has no trade agreement with New Zealand that changes this.

workedExamples.title: Rennet casein from Canada, USMCA-qualifying
workedExamples.body: Casein is Free under the general rate and a USMCA claim removes Canada's 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93). But casein is on the **Section 338 dairy list** (U.S. note 51(b)(2), 9903.03.13), and that 50% applies **whether or not** the goods qualify for USMCA. A $100,000 entry pays **$50,000**; without a USMCA claim it pays $60,000 (50% + 10%).

workedExamples.title: Pea protein isolate from China
workedExamples.body: Protein isolates pay **5%** general, plus **7.5%** Section 301 List 4A (9903.88.15) and **12.5%** 2026 Section 301 (9903.05.31) — **25%** in tariffs. On top, high-protein pea protein is under **antidumping and countervailing duty orders** (89 FR 68390): the China-wide antidumping cash deposit is 269.77% and the all-others countervailing rate 15.84%, unless the exporter has its own rate. The calculator shows only the 25%.

workedExamples.title: Industrial enzymes from Denmark
workedExamples.body: Enzymes are **Free** under the general rate. EU goods pay the 2026 Section 301 rate as a floor: 10% replaces any lower base rate (U.S. note 52, 9903.05.39), so the total is **10%** — $10,000 on a $100,000 entry. If the enzymes are for pharmaceutical use, note 52(e) exempts them (9903.05.89) and the duty is $0.

seo.title: HTS Chapter 35 Tariff Updates 2026 — Casein, Whey, Gelatin, Glue & Enzyme Duties Since 2025 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 35 imports since January 2025: the IEEPA duties and their end, the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and Brazil, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on casein, whey and gelatin, China's Section 301 lists and the pea protein and capsule AD/CVD orders — with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 35 base rate changed**; five statistical lines were added (pea protein, organic and other; other proteins; and a split of other enzymes).

The extra duties changed a lot. In 2025 non-USMCA goods from Canada and Mexico paid IEEPA duties, Chinese goods paid IEEPA duties on top of the older Section 301 lists, and every other country paid the reciprocal tariff — no Chapter 35 line was exempt. All IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and a 10% Section 122 surcharge applied until July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** reach all 33 lines from 60 economies (only enzymes for pharmaceutical use are exempt), Brazil pays 37.5%, and since **August 22, 2026** Canada's casein, whey protein, gelatin, protein isolates and modified starches pay a **50% Section 338 duty**, USMCA or not.

Antidumping and countervailing duties on **pea protein from China** and on **hard empty capsules** (which may be entered as gelatin) are listed for reference; they are company-specific and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 35 from any country — the 2026 Section 301 action on 60 economies and on Brazil, Canada's Section 338 duties, China's Section 301 lists 3 and 4A, the Russia-only Section 232 aluminum and column 2 measures, and the ended IEEPA, Section 122 and Section 232 derivative duties — plus the antidumping and countervailing duty orders that cover Chapter 35 goods, which the tariff calculator does not model. For the total each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

changes.title: No Chapter 35 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 28 lines that exist in both editions carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. Five statistical lines are new and take their 8-digit parent's rate: pea protein, certified organic and other (3504.00.50.10, .50.50), other proteins (3504.00.50.80), and a split of other enzymes into proteases, amylases, lipases, cellulases, pectinases, oxidases and catalases (3507.90.70.10) and others (3507.90.70.80).

changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that pay the column 1-general rate (that is, not entered under CAFTA-DR) will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. CAFTA-DR originating goods are not covered (U.S. note 29). Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.detail: From September 29, 2026 certain Canadian dairy products, alcoholic beverages and motorcycles moved from the 50% Section 338 duty to an import ban. No Chapter 35 line is on the ban lists: Canadian casein, caseinates and whey protein stay at 50%.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duties cover 13 Chapter 35 subheadings
changes.detail: 50% on products of Canada took effect after a 3-day suspension lapsed. changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover all of Chapter 35
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries

changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025, and an additional duty on goods of China (9903.01.20) from February 4, 2025 — including all Chapter 35 goods. Ended February 24, 2026.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 35 goods were **$3.95B in 2025**, down 1.6% from $4.01B in 2024 and below the 2022 peak of $4.84B. No single supplier dominates: 82 countries shipped, and the top two — **Denmark** ($452M) and **China** ($362M) — had about a fifth of the total.

Each product has its own supply base. **Enzymes** ($960M, 24% of the chapter) come mainly from Denmark ($247M), Japan, Germany, Finland and France. **Casein and caseinates** ($524M) come from New Zealand ($192M), Ireland, Denmark and France; **whey protein isolates** (milk albumin, $232M, up from $181M) and other albumins mainly from Denmark, New Zealand and the UK. **Other proteins** — collagen, pea protein, peptones — ($796M) come from Brazil ($189M), China ($144M) and Canada ($119M). **Adhesives** ($748M) come from Germany ($201M), Mexico ($94M) and Canada; **modified starches** ($384M) from China, Thailand and Australia; **gelatin** ($273M, down from $321M) from Brazil, Canada, China, France and Argentina.

The duty picture changed only after these figures: since July and August 2026 nearly all of these suppliers pay the 2026 Section 301 tariffs, Brazil 37.5%, and most of Canada's casein, albumin, gelatin, protein and starch trade (headings 3501–3505, $163M in 2025) is on the 50% Section 338 lists. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 35: Albuminoidal Substances, Modified Starches, Glues & Enzymes — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Gelatin, Casein, Whey Protein, Enzymes & Adhesives: FDA, APHIS, TSCA Rules & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 35) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 35 line — FDA prior notice and FSVP for food proteins and gelatin, APHIS permits for casein and animal-derived proteins, FSIS for egg albumin, TSCA certification for adhesives and industrial enzymes — the pea protein and capsule AD/CVD orders, and the legal ways to pay less.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Chapter 35 goods are mostly food and pharmaceutical ingredients or industrial chemicals, so **which agency signs off depends on the use**. Food-grade casein, whey protein, egg albumin, gelatin, collagen, pea protein, modified food starch and food enzymes are FDA-regulated foods (registration, prior notice, FSVP); animal-derived ones can also need USDA APHIS clearance, and dried egg albumin USDA FSIS. Adhesives, industrial starches and industrial enzymes need a TSCA certification.

With base rates this low, the money is in the **extra duties**: the right origin and USMCA claim, the pharmaceutical-use exemption for enzymes, the right classification (a binding ruling), staying outside the pea protein and capsule AD/CVD orders, and drawback on goods you export. Each rule and lever below links to its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods from Canada or Mexico
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty plus the base rate (up to 6.5%, or 47.6¢/kg on dried egg albumin). For Canada it does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on the 13 listed subheadings.
levers.appliesTo: All 33 lines, for goods that meet the Chapter 35 rules of origin in General Note 11
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer. It need not follow a prescribed format; it can be on the invoice or another document, and CBP can ask for it.
levers.caveat: Canadian casein, caseinates, whey protein, egg albumin, gelatin, protein isolates and modified starches pay 50% under Section 338 even with a USMCA claim (U.S. note 51(a)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 51 and 52
USTR statement on the USMCA joint review (July 1, 2026)

levers.title: Claim another free trade agreement or AGOA
levers.saves: The base rate — for example 5% on protein isolates, 6.5% on retail animal glue, 47.6¢/kg on dried egg albumin — on goods from Australia, Bahrain, Chile, Colombia, Israel, Jordan, South Korea, Morocco, Oman, Panama, Peru, Singapore, the CAFTA-DR countries and AGOA beneficiaries
levers.appliesTo: The 25 dutiable lines (the 8 Free lines have no base rate to remove)
levers.document: The origin proof each agreement requires (a certification or declaration of origin) and records to back it up.
levers.caveat: An FTA removes the base rate but not the 2026 Section 301 duty, which applies even when a special rate is claimed (U.S. note 52(a)); for South Korea the 12.5% floor applies anyway. AGOA runs through December 31, 2026; GSP (A, A*, A+) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Declare enzymes for pharmaceutical use
levers.saves: The whole 2026 Section 301 duty (10%–12.5%) and, for Brazil, the 25% duty too
levers.appliesTo: 3507.90.70 (other enzymes) for use in pharmaceutical applications
levers.document: Enter under 9903.05.89 (and 9903.05.06 for Brazil) with records showing the pharmaceutical use, such as the purchaser's drug-manufacturing use and specifications.
levers.caveat: Only enzymes actually for pharmaceutical applications qualify; industrial and food enzymes pay the duty. It does not remove China's 25% List 3 duty.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 52(e) and 50(a)(v)

levers.title: Get the classification right — ask CBP for a binding ruling
levers.saves: The gap between neighboring lines: whey protein isolate (3502.20) is Free, protein isolates 5% (3504.00.10), other proteins 4%; casein (3501.10.50) Free vs caseinates 0.37¢/kg; optically clear adhesives (3506.91.10) Free vs 2.1%. Classification also decides whether Canada's Section 338 list, a China list or an AD/CVD order applies.
levers.appliesTo: All 33 lines, especially protein powders, collagen and milk protein products
levers.document: A binding ruling request to CBP with the product's composition, protein content and use (19 CFR part 177). For example, CBP has ruled bovine collagen powder into 3504.00.50 (N301872), whey protein isolate 90 into 3502.20 (N282570), pea protein isolate into 3504.00.10 (N359602) and a milk protein isolate into 3504.00.10 (N020518).
levers.caveat: A ruling binds only the product described. Note 2 sends dextrins with more than 10% reducing sugar to heading 1702, and flavored protein shake mixes are classified outside Chapter 35 (a protein shake mix went to 1806.90.90 in N309121).

levers.title: Know the country of origin
levers.saves: Up to 37.5 percentage points: the same Free-rated enzyme pays 10% from the EU, 12.5% from Japan, 37.5% from Brazil or China (List 3), and nothing from Mexico under USMCA
levers.document: Production records showing where the goods were made. For proteins processed in several countries, origin follows the last substantial transformation; CBP's 2026 ruling N359602 on pea protein isolate refined in Cambodia from Chinese concentrate is an example.
levers.caveat: Origin for tariffs and the scope of an AD/CVD order are decided separately: the pea protein orders cover Chinese pea protein blended in third countries.

citations.label: CBP ruling N359602 (origin of pea protein isolate)
HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 50, 51 and 52

levers.title: Check the AD/CVD scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping and countervailing duty when the product is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: Pea protein from China (3504.00.10, 3504.00.50); hard empty capsules from Brazil, China, India and Vietnam (entered under 3503.00.55.10 or 9602)
levers.document: The order's written scope. The pea protein orders cover pea protein of at least 65% protein (dry weight) and exclude textured pea protein, pea protein crisps, chickpea protein, finished foods such as bars and baked goods, and blends with less than 5% high-protein pea protein. When unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.
levers.caveat: A product inside the scope pays the cash deposit whatever HTS line it is entered under, and AD/CVD are not refundable through drawback.

levers.title: Recover duty on goods you export
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid — including the Section 301 and Section 338 duties — when the imported goods, or goods made from them, are exported or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: Any line, for example adhesives or proteins used in exported products
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import and export records (19 CFR part 191).
levers.caveat: Antidumping and countervailing duties are not subject to drawback (19 CFR 191.3(b)(3)). Claims have filing deadlines and record-keeping rules.

rules.title: Food-grade products: the foreign facility that makes or packs them must be registered with FDA
Food-grade products: prior notice to FDA before the shipment arrives
Food-grade products: the U.S. importer needs a foreign supplier verification program (FSVP)
Modified food starch: only the treatments and limits listed for food starch-modified may be used in food

Cattle-derived food and cosmetic ingredients: the importer affirms at entry that no prohibited cattle materials are used (gelatin and milk products are not prohibited cattle materials) and keeps records
Casein, caseinates and lactalbumin from regions with foot-and-mouth disease: only with written APHIS permission

Animal-derived proteins (processed animal protein, including hydrolyzed proteins such as collagen peptides, and their derivatives): prohibited unless an exception applies; usually a VS permit (VS Form 16-3) and a veterinary certificate
Dried and other egg albumin (egg products): only from countries FSIS has found eligible, with a foreign inspection certificate, and reinspected at an official import establishment
Adhesives, industrial starches and industrial enzymes: TSCA import certification (positive or negative) at entry
Pea protein from China: antidumping (China-wide cash deposit 269.77%) and countervailing duty (all others 15.84%) orders — not in the tariff calculator
Hard empty (gelatin) capsules from Brazil, China, India and Vietnam: antidumping and countervailing duty orders — not in the tariff calculator

groups.label: Casein, caseinates & casein glues
groups.note: Food-grade casein, caseinates and milk protein concentrate follow FDA food rules; from foot-and-mouth disease regions they need written APHIS permission (9 CFR 94.16(b)(3)). Casein glues (3501.90.20) are chemicals and need a TSCA certification. All four subheadings pay Canada's 50% Section 338 duty.

groups.label: Albumins: egg white & whey protein isolate
groups.note: Egg albumin is an egg product: FSIS allows it only from eligible countries with a foreign inspection certificate. Milk albumin and whey protein isolates follow the FDA food rules and APHIS's milk-product rule (lactalbumin is named in 9 CFR 94.16(b)(3)).

groups.label: Gelatin & animal glue
groups.note: Edible gelatin follows FDA food rules; bovine gelatin is not a prohibited cattle material, but the importer must affirm compliance at entry. Inedible gelatin and animal glue are chemicals (TSCA). Hard gelatin capsules from Brazil, China, India and Vietnam are under AD/CVD orders whatever line they are entered under.

groups.label: Peptones & other proteins (collagen, pea protein)
groups.note: Collagen, collagen peptides, peptones and other animal-derived proteins fall under APHIS's processed-animal-protein rules (hydrolyzed proteins are named in 9 CFR 95.1). Pea protein from China (3504.00.10, 3504.00.50) is under AD/CVD orders.

groups.label: Dextrins, modified starches & starch glues
groups.note: Modified food starch must meet 21 CFR 172.892; starches and starch glues for paper, textiles or adhesives are chemicals and need a TSCA certification.

groups.label: Prepared glues & adhesives
groups.note: Prepared glues and adhesives are chemical mixtures: TSCA certification at entry. Russian-origin adhesives of four subheadings pay the 200% aluminum derivative duty and three pay 35% under Proclamation 10420.

groups.label: Enzymes
groups.note: Food enzymes follow FDA food rules; industrial enzymes (detergent, textile, feed processing) need a TSCA certification; enzymes for medicines are FDA drug ingredients and can use the pharmaceutical-use Section 301 exemption.

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations — not legal advice. AD/CVD rates are company-specific and change with each administrative review; check Commerce's latest notice and CBP's cash-deposit instructions before importing. Which agency rules apply depends on the product's source and intended use.

seo.title: HTS Chapter 35 FAQ: HS Codes for Gelatin, Collagen, Casein, Whey Protein, Glue & Enzymes + 2026 Tariffs | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about HTS Chapter 35: HS codes for gelatin, gelatin capsules, collagen, casein, whey protein, pea protein, egg albumin, modified starch, glue and enzymes, and the 2026 tariffs on whey protein and protein powder.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common searches about HTS Chapter 35 — which HS code a product falls under and what it pays today. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 35 base rates are low — 8 of 33 lines are Free, most others 2–6% or a few cents per kilogram — but no line is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 tariffs: EU goods pay 10% in total, Japan and Korea 12.5%, New Zealand and Australia +12.5%, Brazil +37.5%, China +20% or +37.5%.

Canadian casein, caseinates, whey protein, egg albumin, gelatin, protein isolates and modified starches pay a 50% Section 338 duty since August 22, 2026, even when they qualify for USMCA; Canadian adhesives and enzymes and USMCA goods from Mexico are Free.

The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026. Pea protein from China and hard gelatin capsules from Brazil, China, India and Vietnam carry antidumping and countervailing duties that the tariff calculator does not include.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 35 (albuminoidal substances)?
faqs.answer: Chapter 35 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers albuminoidal (protein) substances and related products: casein and caseinates (3501), albumins such as egg white and whey protein isolate (3502), gelatin and animal glue (3503), peptones and other proteins such as collagen and pea protein (3504), dextrins and modified starches (3505), prepared glues and adhesives (3506) and enzymes (3507) — 33 ten-digit U.S. lines. The U.S. imported $3.95B of them in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for gelatin?
faqs.answer: 3503.00. Edible gelatin, whether bovine, porcine or fish, in sheets or powder, is 3503.00.55.10; photographic gelatin 3503.00.55.20; other gelatin 3503.00.55.50 — all 2.8¢/kg + 3.8%. Inedible gelatin and animal glue is 3503.00.20 (under 88¢/kg, 1.2¢/kg + 3.2%) or 3503.00.40 (88¢/kg or more), and fish glue 3503.00.10. Canadian gelatin of 3503.00.40 and 3503.00.55 pays 50% under Section 338; EU gelatin 10% in total; Brazilian gelatin the base rate plus 37.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for empty gelatin capsules, and are there duties on them?
searchedAs: hs code for empty gelatin capsules
hs code for empty hard gelatin capsules
faqs.answer: Commerce's 2026 orders describe hard empty capsules as classifiable in 9602.00.10.40 and 9602.00.50.10, and note that gelatin capsules may also be entered under 3503.00.55.10. Whichever line is used, capsules from Brazil, China, India and Vietnam are under antidumping and countervailing duty orders since February 2026: antidumping cash deposits of 77.63% (Brazil), 18.71% (China), 11.70% (India, all others) and 46.24% (Vietnam), plus countervailing duties of 2.45%–10.67%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for collagen or collagen peptides?
faqs.answer: Collagen and collagen peptides as an ingredient are generally 3504.00.50 — other protein substances and their derivatives, 4% general. CBP classified bovine collagen gel and powder there in ruling N301872. Collagen mixed into a finished supplement or drink can fall in another chapter, so check CBP rulings or ask for one. Brazilian collagen pays the base rate plus 37.5%, Chinese +20%, Canadian 3504.00.50 goods 50% under Section 338.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for casein and sodium caseinate?
faqs.answer: 3501. Casein — rennet or acid — is 3501.10.50 (Free); milk protein concentrate, meaning any complete milk protein (casein plus lactalbumin) concentrate, is 3501.10.10 (0.37¢/kg); sodium, calcium and other caseinates are 3501.90.60 (0.37¢/kg); casein glues 3501.90.20 (6%). New Zealand casein pays the base rate plus 12.5%, EU casein 10% in total, and Canadian casein 50% under Section 338 even with USMCA.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for whey protein isolate or concentrate?
searchedAs: hs code for whey protein isolate
faqs.answer: Whey protein concentrates with more than 80% whey protein on a dry basis, including isolates, are 3502.20.00 (milk albumin), Free under the general rate; CBP ruled whey protein isolate 90 there (N282570). Lower-protein whey protein concentrates and whey powder are classified in Chapter 4 (heading 0404), not Chapter 35.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on whey protein imports?
faqs.answer: The base rate on whey protein isolate (3502.20) is Free, but the 2026 extra duties apply: New Zealand +12.5%, the EU 10% in total, the UK +10%, Canada 50% under Section 338 (with or without USMCA), China +20%. USMCA-qualifying Mexican whey protein is Free. The U.S. imported $232M of it in 2025.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on protein powder?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on protein powder
faqs.answer: It depends on the classification. Whey protein isolate is 3502.20 (Free base), pea, soy and other protein isolates 3504.00.10 (5%), other proteins 3504.00.50 (4%) — each plus the 2026 Section 301 duty for the country. Flavored or blended shake mixes are usually classified outside Chapter 35: CBP put a protein shake mix from China in 1806.90.90 (ruling N309121). Pea protein from China also pays antidumping and countervailing duties.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for pea protein, and is there an antidumping duty on Chinese pea protein?
faqs.answer: Pea protein isolate is 3504.00.10 (5%; CBP ruling N359602, 2026); other pea protein is 3504.00.50.10 (certified organic) or 3504.00.50.50 (4%). Since August 2024, high-protein pea protein (65% or more) from China is under antidumping and countervailing duty orders: 269.77% China-wide antidumping cash deposit (111.65% for separate-rate exporters) and 15.84% countervailing for all others — on top of 5% + 7.5% List 4A + 12.5% Section 301.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for enzymes?
faqs.answer: 3507. Rennet is 3507.10; penicillin G amidase 3507.90.20; other enzymes and prepared enzymes 3507.90.70 — proteases, amylases, lipases, cellulases, pectinases, oxidases and catalases under statistical suffix 10, others under 80. All are Free under the general rate. Enzymatic pre-tanning and washing preparations and enzyme medicaments are excluded (Chapters 32, 34 and 30). Danish enzymes pay 10% in total; Chinese +37.5%; enzymes for pharmaceutical use are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for glue and adhesives?
faqs.answer: Mostly 3506. Glues put up for retail sale in packs of up to 1 kg (glue sticks, super glue) are 3506.10 — animal glue 6.5%, others 2.1%; adhesives based on plastics polymers or rubber are 3506.91 (2.1%, optically clear adhesives Free); other prepared adhesives 3506.99 (2.1%). Starch glues are 3505.20, casein glues 3501.90.20, animal glue in bulk 3503.00. Self-adhesive plastic tape and labels are not Chapter 35. Chinese adhesives pay +37.5%, German 10% in total.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for modified starch and dextrin?
faqs.answer: 3505.10.00 (0.7¢/kg) covers dextrins and modified starches such as pregelatinized, esterified or etherified starch: dextrin from potato starch .15, other dextrin .20; other modified starch from corn .40, from potato .45, other (for example tapioca) .92. Under Chapter 35 note 2, dextrins with more than 10% reducing sugar — which can include maltodextrin — belong in heading 1702. Starch glues are 3505.20.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for egg albumin or egg white powder?
faqs.answer: Dried egg albumin (egg white powder) is 3502.11.00 at 47.6¢/kg; other egg albumin 3502.19.00 at 9.7¢/kg. As egg products they can enter only from countries USDA FSIS has found eligible, with a foreign inspection certificate. Dried egg albumin from China pays +37.5%, from Canada +50% under Section 338.
